newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 2.03 pct lower on finance worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 2.03 pct lower on finance worries.

text.p: Persistent concerns over the future of financial companies plus a run on deposits at some banks and finance firms prompted investors to sell and drove the index down 2.03 percent on Wednesday, brokers said.
The composite SET index closed 13.15 points lower at 635.32 on about five billion baht turnover.

"Many depositors at the 42 finance companies ordered suspended by the government were still confused and not certain they would get their money back. As worries mounted many depositors withdrew their money from financial institutions still in operation," said Bumnan Liumsuwan of Asia Credit.
Brokers said many depositors also withdrew their money from small banks after the government late on Wednesday gave a surprise order suspending 42 cash-strapped finance companies.
A similar action was taken by the government in late June when 16 finance companies were ordered suspended.
Brokers said investors were concerned despite assurances from authorities that depositors should not be worried.

The finance minister and central bank governor assured investors that all deposits at non-suspended finance companies and commercial banks were fully insured. On Tuesday the government said creditors and depositors of the troubled firms would be fully protected.
The suspension of 42 ailing finance companies was part of the government's restrictive measures to remedy the economy following recommendations of the IMF.

Brokers said the government's decision on Tuesday to hike the valued added tax to 10 percent from seven percent also worried investors as they thought the increase might affect prices of public utilities later on.
All the major counters retreated with the banking sector topping it in terms of value, falling 2.97 percent.

Bangkok Bank topped the active list in terms of value, losing six baht to 168. Dhana Siam Finance declined 2.50 to 33.50 and Eastern Water Resources Development and Management gained five to 55.00. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642, email:bangkok.newsroom@reuters.com
